newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani police crack down on political activists.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani police crack down on political activists.

text.p: Pakistani police have arrested 54 political activists of an ethnic group to try to stem growing violence in the southern port city of Karachi, police said on Friday.
One official confirmed the 54 arrests, but did not identify the activists.
A spokesman for the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) Haqqiqi group said police had arrested more than 350 of its activists in the last two days.
Police did not confirm the MQM-Haqqiqi claim but said those it had detained had been picked in the past two days.
Violence between the MQM, led by London-based Altaf Hussain, and its splinter faction MQM-Haqqiqi has risen since national and provincial elections on February 3.

After the elections, the MQM allied itself with with Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League to form a coalition government in Sindh, the home province of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto.
Both groups have accused each other of involvement in violence. Hussain has repeatedly urged the government to take action against his opponents who he blames for the violence.
A spokesman for MQM-Haqqiqi condemned what he called "the indiscriminate raids and arrests of more than 350 of its workers and sympathisers by the police without any valid reason".
More than 800 people were killed in ethnic, political and sectarian strife in Karachi last year, compared with more than 2,000 in 1995.
